subject: Critical Thinking
title: Formal vs. Informal Fallacies
description: A 60-second lesson on Formal vs. Informal Fallacies.

hook.text: Some fallacies break the rules of logic itself. Others play by the rules but cheat with content. Both are deadly.

buildup.text: Formal fallacies: the logical structure is invalid. 'If A then B; B; therefore A' – wrong regardless of what A & B are.

discovery.text: Informal fallacies: the structure may be valid, but the content is flawed – irrelevant evidence, hidden assumptions.

twist.text: Most real-world fallacies are informal. Nobody argues in pure syllogisms – they argue in stories, analogies, & emotions.

climax.text: Formal fallacies are detectable by machines. Informal fallacies require human judgment — which is itself biased.

punchline.text: Logic errors are easy to catch. Persuasion errors are not.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between formal and informal fallacies?
options: Formal have flawed structure; informal have flawed content
Informal are only used in debates

details.summary: Formal fallacies violate the rules of logical structure, making an argument invalid regardless of its content. Informal fallacies use flawed reasoning despite technically correct structure, relying on misleading content or context.
details.whyItMatters: Distinguishing formal from informal fallacies helps you identify whether the flaw is in the logic itself or in how the premises are being used.
takeaways: Formal fallacies fail due to structural errors in logic
Informal fallacies fail due to misleading content or context
Most everyday fallacies are informal rather than formal

faq.question: Can you give examples of both a formal and an informal fallacy?
faq.answer: Formal: affirming the consequent — 'If it rains, the ground is wet. The ground is wet, so it rained.' Informal: ad hominem — 'You cannot trust his argument because he is unpleasant.' The first has a structural flaw; the second has a content flaw.

faq.question: Which type of fallacy is more common in everyday arguments?
faq.answer: Informal fallacies are far more common because everyday arguments rarely use strict logical form. Appeals to emotion, irrelevant authority, and hasty generalizations dominate real-world discourse.
